text: The AWS Glue Data Catalog — AWS's central metadata repository, shared by Glue, Athena, Redshift Spectrum, and EMR.
A crawler is the AWS equivalent of a Purview scan. It connects to a source, usually S3, infers schema from the actual files, and writes or updates table definitions.
The resulting table page shows the inferred schema and an S3 location — confirming this is pure metadata pointing at data, not a copy of the data itself.
Four crawler runs later, the same table's comments carry sensitive-data classification — EMAIL and SSN flags written by an automated detection job.
Three concepts: a database is just a namespace. A table is schema and location metadata. A crawler is what keeps both of those current.
Next up: AWS Lake Formation — permissions layered directly on top of the catalog you just saw.
